newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA, Aug 5 - Vancouver, B.C. - Average waiting times for grain loading at Vancouver and Prince Rupert 3-4 days. There are no delays for coal loading at Prince Rupert. Roberts Bank - 24 Vessels in line-up for Aug. Waiting times can be greater than the present 2-3 days expected towards the end of the month. Neptune coal terminal - A possibility of 1-2 days waiting.

HONDURAS, Aug 4 - Puerto Cortes - Six vessels berthed of which 2 discharging wheat, 2 bananas/containers. 2 Discharging/loading containers. 4 Vessels awaiting berths of which 3 to discharge/load containers, 1 to discharge wheat. 15 Vessels due of which 5 to discharge bananas, 1 to discharge wheat, 9 to load/discharge containers. Puerto Cortes - Five vessels berthed of which 3 discharging/loading containers/general cargo, 2 discharging wheat. 1 Anchored to discharge steel products. 20 Vessels due of which 2 to discharge (1 lpg, 1 liquid chemicals). 16 To discharge/load (10 containers/general cargo, 6 containers/bananas). 1 To load lumber, 1 passenger vessel.

MEXICO, Aug 5 - All ports working normally. Tampico - Seven vessels in port of which 1 coke, 1 steel coils, 1 steel plates, 2 cement, 1 fuel, 1 gasoline. Altamira - Two container vessels in port. Veracruz - 11 Vessels in port of which 2 general cargo, 2 containers, 2 wheat, 3 corn, 2 under repair. Manzanillo - 10 Vessels in port of which 2 clinker, 3 containers, 2 general cargo, 1 cement, 2 grains. Coatzacoalcos - 14 Vessels in port of which 9 chemicals, 5 oil tankers.

UNITED STATES, Aug 4 - Hampton Roads, VA - Seven general cargo/container vessels berthed and operating, 4 vessels berthed loading coal, 4 anchored waiting to load. 1 Bulker loading fertiliser, 1 discharging gypsum, 1 loading wood-pulp. 2 Vessels berthed under repair.

EAST COAST - Baltimore, MD - Dundalk terminal - No congestion expected this week. Elevators, liquid bulk facilities and coal operations - Working normally with no delays. Consol Coal - Average waiting time 3 days. Anchorages available at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - No delays at any of the container terminals or grain elevators. Grain elevator - On a first-come-first-served basis. Miami, FL - No berthing delays expected either at Miami or Port Everglades. New York, NY - No congestion at anchorages, no congestion at tanker or sugar terminals. Norfolk, VA - Southern Coal pier - 9 Vessels due during the week. At present there are 3 vessels anchored waiting to load. Dominion terminal - 10 Vessels due. Pier IX terminal - 5 Vessels due during the week. Maintenae has been completed on Southern Coal pier 6 and both loaders are again operating. Cargill - 1 Vessel due during the week. Container, general cargo, oil and bulk terminals - All working normally. All channels open with prevailing depths available. Philadelphia, PA - No congestion at Philadelphia, Camden or Wilmington. No navigational/dredging problems.

GULF COAST - Houston, TX - No congestion at city docks, public grain elevator or Cargill elevator. However, congestion exists at Farmland grain elevator, Galveston where there is approx. 2-3 days waiting, also for some chemical terminals. New Orleans, LA - Seasonal rains may cause delays to cargo operations, especially grain loading. Grain shipments normal for the season. River stage at 3.6 ft. Bar pilots advise that the draft for the Mississippi River gulf outlet will be 36 ft. Present max. permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 47 ft. Fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt., 46 ft. Fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt.

WEST COAST - Columbia river - Grain vessel activity seems to be increasing. There are 14 grain vessels in port, of which 5 loading and 9 waiting at anchor. Coos Bay, OR - No vessels at present, port slow. No delays. Three vessels due of which 1 wood-chip carrier at Roseburg chip terminal, 1 to discharge nickel at Glenbrook nickel dock and 1 due at export service to load lumber. Deepening of upper channel continues but no delays to vessel traffic. Honolulu, HI - The southerly swells, which last week delayed several vessels attempting to bunker at the anchorages, have subsided. This week's forecast is for easterly trade winds, which should cause no delays to bunkering vessels.
